noah: Quick one 1: a user hit a runtime crash on Cloudflare Workers. ESM entry pulled our normal bundle and crashed due to Buffer/crypto usage.

iti: Oof. Do we have an edge-specific bundle? I thought our exports had an edge condition but maybe the published package missed it.

marie: We added an "edge" condition in the draft PR but didn't include a `./edge` subpath. Workers sometimes resolve differently; adding explicit `exports['./edge']` helps devs import the exact variant.

noah: Proposed minimal change: ship `dist/esm/edge.mjs`, add `exports.{".":{"edge":"dist/esm/edge.mjs","import":"dist/esm/node.mjs","require":"dist/cjs/index.js","types":"dist/types/index.d.ts"},"./edge":{"import":"dist/esm/edge.mjs","types":"dist/types/index.d.ts"}}`, and keep `types` top-level.

iti: Also ensure the edge bundle doesn't reference `process` or `node:crypto`. Small runtime shim for auth-retry should use `globalThis.crypto` and `fetch` only.

marie: CI: I'll add a tiny Cloudflare Wrangler smoke test that `import Client from 'redwood-sdk/edge'` in a worker and performs an auth flow. Fail on ReferenceError or Buffer complaints.

ci-bot: canary published -> redwood-sdk-canary-1723456789; smoke job queued -> canary-edge-wrangler/1723456789

noah: Thanks. If this lands quickly, we should update quickstart to show `import {createClient} from 'redwood-sdk/edge'` so onboarding is clearer.
